questions.q: What are the three distinct states a Payables transaction's accounting passes through?
options: Created, validated, matched
Accounted, transferred, posted
Drafted, approved, cancelled
Selected, proposed, built
questions.explain: A transaction is first accounted in Payables (Final mode), then transferred to GL as an unposted batch, then posted to update balances.

questions.q: What is true of a journal batch immediately after being transferred to GL, but before posting?
options: The entries exist in GL but account balances have not yet changed
Account balances have already been updated
The batch is automatically deleted
It is sent back to Payables for re-accounting
questions.explain: A transferred-but-unposted batch exists in GL, but balances only update once the batch is posted.

questions.q: What are the two ways accounting entries can move from Payables to General Ledger?
options: Only through a manual journal entry typed directly in GL
Only by exporting to a spreadsheet and re-importing
Create Accounting with the Transfer to GL option selected, or a separate Transfer Journal Entries to GL program
Only automatically overnight with no option to run on demand
questions.explain: The transfer can be combined into the Create Accounting run itself, or handled afterward by a standalone transfer program.

questions.q: In the Solace Robotics example, what is true of the two journal batches right after the transfer?
options: They are already posted and reflected in account balances
They were automatically merged into a single batch
They were rejected due to an accounting error
They are unposted and still need review and posting by a GL accountant
questions.explain: The batches arrive in GL unposted; a GL accountant reviews and posts them before balances are updated.

questions.q: Why is it useful to keep "accounted," "transferred," and "posted" as separate, visible states?
options: It has no practical benefit and only adds complexity
It lets someone pinpoint exactly which stage a discrepancy occurred at during reconciliation
It is required only for tax reporting purposes
It prevents Payables from ever generating accounting entries
questions.explain: Visible, distinct states make it possible to trace a reconciliation mismatch to a specific stage rather than treating the whole process as a black box.
